properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-09-16, in his words: *"Secondly, need to ensure that designs 'close' and are verified."*

"Closes" is his word from systems engineering, and it means something definite there: the requirements are all allocated and traced, every one has a verification that passes, the resource budgets (mass, power, cost, schedule, margin) sum inside their limits, every interface is specified on both sides, and nothing the increment depends on is still undecided. A design that closes can be built; one that does not has a named hole.

═══ WHAT THE GRAPH ALREADY COMPUTES, piece by piece ═══
· The delivery line — "Delivered: N of M requirements", computed from the thread (satisfied, realized, passing check), never from a status field. That is the traceability leg of closure.
· budget_report — constraints with quantity/limit/direction summed against their limits. That is the budget leg, where budgets are modelled (on reflow2's own design: barely).
· seam_coverage / seam_report — couplings through a declared interface, and whether both sides specified it. The interface leg.
· what_next and loop_status — open decisions and what the loop owes. The decision leg.
· maturity_report — seven bands and a frontier, deliberately NOT a verdict ("a demonstrator may sit at 40% forever and be right").
· readiness gating — a ReadinessAssessment against a threshold the owner states on a GATED_ON edge, never defaulted.
What is missing is not any leg; it is ONE READ that puts them together and says, against a threshold the owner declared, whether the design closes — and names the first hole when it does not.

═══ THE OPTIONS, none chosen ═══
A. ⭐ A CLOSURE REPORT: one call, five legs, one verdict. Requirements traced-and-passing over live requirements; budgets inside limit with the stated margin; boundaries specified both sides; open decisions the increment is scheduled on; quantities with no source (the sibling idea). Each leg reports its count and its worst offender; the verdict is computed against a closure threshold the project declared (100% is a legal declaration; so is "traceability and budgets only, seams are not modelled here"). ⚠️ Cost: a threshold nobody declared must read as "no closure criterion stated", never as a default — that is the readiness ruling, and it is the whole difficulty: five legs means five thresholds or one owner-written rule.
B. CLOSURE AS THE RELEASE GATE. A cut is refused (or reported, per dec:release-trigger) while the design does not close at the declared threshold. ⚠️ Counter: reflow2 itself would not close today — 38 gaps never asked, one capability with no passing check — and it ships; a gate that forbids what the owner does is a gate the owner turns off.
C. CLOSURE PER INCREMENT, NOT PER DESIGN. What closes is the set of things scheduled into an epoch; the design as a whole never closes while it is alive. arrival_delta already reads what an epoch delivered against what was scheduled; closure would add "and did all of it verify, and did the budgets it touched hold". ⚠️ Counter: a building closes as a whole or the permit is refused; per-increment closure is the software habit reasserting itself.
D. NOTHING NEW — the reports exist; the person assembles the verdict. ⚠️ Counter: the where-am-i skill has a written lesson that a session read the delivery line, never said it, and recomputed it by hand hours later; five reports assembled by hand is the same failure five times.

═══ THE HONEST LIMIT ═══
A closure verdict is only as true as the legs it sums: a budget nobody modelled reads as "inside limit" for want of a limit, and a requirement nobody wrote is not missing from the count. The verdict must therefore say what it swept, the way detect_defects does — "budgets: 1 modelled; seams: 13 of 72 declared" — or it is the vacuous green this project keeps finding.
properties.name: OPEN — what does it mean for a design to CLOSE, and should reflow2 compute that verdict — every requirement traced to a passing check, every budget inside its limit with margin, every boundary specified on both sides, no open decision the increment needs — against a closure threshold the owner declares?
properties.rationale: Captured under the brainstorm skill, nothing promoted. Kept separate from the readiness ruling because readiness asks "is this mature enough to field" and closure asks "is this design complete enough to build", which are different questions with the same threshold discipline. Every leg named here already has a computation behind it; the idea is the single read and the declared threshold, and the counter-argument that reflow2 itself would not close is recorded because it is the strongest argument against making closure a gate.
